analysis.title: Talen Energy Corp. (TLN): Updating estimates ahead of 3Q; upcoming guidance update and PJM dynamics in focus
key_insights: GS refreshes its Talen Energy (TLN, Buy) model for latest commodity prices and capital allocation activity ahead of 3Q results. 12-month price target cut to $501 from $509, implying 48.3% upside from $337.78.

GS expects TLN to give a financial guidance update on the 3Q call that points to upside versus Street estimates, helped by the accelerated share repurchase (ASR), which supports FCF/share despite higher near-term interest expense.
GS sees TLN as the most PJM-levered IPP to capacity prices, which differentiates it among publicly traded independent power producers.
GS does not expect an explicit data center PPA announcement with results. It expects updates on PJM capacity auctions, large load and local basis.

Guidance expectations: updated 2026/2027 guidance, a refreshed FCF/share outlook for 2027/2028, and new 2029 guidance. GS also expects updated modeling disclosures on O&M expense, capex, capacity revenues and energy margins, consistent with the September 2025 update.
Recent PJM regulatory developments support higher power prices, which GS expects to drive a positive guidance revision versus Street estimates.

Zonal basis is a key investor focus. West Hub pricing is rising faster than PPL zone pricing, so the basis keeps widening, although power prices in the region are all trending higher. GS expects commentary on northern PJM transmission upgrades and load growth to indicate the timing of the discount narrowing.
On the December PJM auction for the 2029/2030 delivery year, GS notes FERC largely rejected the IRAS proposal, which management has called supportive for IPPs because it pushes back on curtailment.
PJM's rejection of the proposal to exclude incremental new large loads from the VRR demand curve used in capacity auction forecasts is viewed as constructive for power prices.

Model changes: the model now includes the $1.5bn ASR and an updated share repurchase program of $3bn through 2028, plus term loans issued in 3Q. GS adjusts zone discount, O&M, G&A and interest expense.
GS projects 3Q26 EBITDA of $701mn versus $699mn previously. 2026-2028 EBITDA estimates move from $2,218mn/$2,826mn/$3,277mn to $2,216mn/$2,828mn/$3,274mn.
Valuation multiples are lowered: target EV/EBITDA on Q5-Q8 estimates goes from 9.5x to 9.25x, and the FCF yield assumption rises from 7.5% to 7.75%.
TLN shares are down 6.1% over 3 months, 7.3% over 6 months and 17.2% over 12 months, underperforming the S&P 500 by 8.8%, 12.9% and 26.2% respectively.

market_movers.rationale: GS cuts the target from $509 to $501 on a lower EV/EBITDA multiple (9.25x from 9.5x), partly offset by a higher FCF yield input (7.75% from 7.5%). It expects a guidance update that points to upside versus Street estimates.

sector_views.rationale: GS rates TLN Buy and sees PJM regulatory developments as supportive of higher power prices for IPPs, with TLN the most PJM-levered to capacity prices.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 earnings upcoming: GS estimates EBITDA of $701mn (prior estimate $699mn). The 3Q result has not been reported yet.
GS 2026E EPS $23.37 (old $22.70), 2027E $31.23 (old $31.62), 2028E $44.46 (old $43.09). These are GS estimates, not Street consensus.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 9/26E $6.62, 12/26E $6.72, 3/27E $7.21. 6/26 EPS shown as $2.37.
GS 2026E-2028E EBITDA is $2,215.8mn/$2,828.0mn/$3,274.2mn, and revenue is $4,697.0mn/$5,241.5mn/$5,704.3mn. 2025 actual EBITDA was $1,035mn and revenue $2,626mn.
GS expects updated 2026/2027 guidance, a refreshed 2027/2028 FCF/share outlook and new 2029 guidance on the call, and a positive revision versus Street estimates.

GS estimates share count falls from 45.7mn (2025) to 41.0mn (2026E), 38.5mn (2027E) and 35.6mn (2028E) on repurchases. Share repurchases are projected at $1,998mn in 2026E, $850mn in 2027E and $1,000mn in 2028E.
risk_factors: Net debt/EBITDA of 5.9x in 2025 and GS-estimated 4.6x in 2026E, with net interest expense of $699.2mn in 2026E, adds leverage and interest cost risk.
